title: Speaking Test 2
summary: Settling into a new neighbourhood, learning a new skill, a busy airport check-in, choosing a weekend getaway, a colleague's mistake, a four-day school week, and an odd piece of furniture.

tasks.label: Task 1: Giving Advice
tasks.prompt: A friend of yours has just moved to a new city with her husband and two children. She says she feels lonely and doesn't know anyone yet. Give her some advice about how to meet people and feel at home.
points: Places or activities where she could meet people
How her children could help the family make connections
How to stay positive while she settles in

tasks.label: Task 2: Talking about a Personal Experience
tasks.prompt: Talk about a time when you learned a new skill, such as driving, cooking, swimming or using a new piece of software.
points: What the skill was and why you wanted to learn it
What was difficult about learning it
How the skill has helped you since

tasks.label: Task 3: Describing a Scene
tasks.prompt: Describe some things that are happening in the picture as well as you can. The person you are speaking to cannot see the picture.

scene.caption: A crowded airport check-in area early on a holiday morning

items.label: A family of four with a cart piled high with suitcases
A man at the counter whose suitcase is on the scale, looking worried
An airline agent pointing at a sign that says "Max 23 kg"
A toddler sitting on a suitcase, crying
A young woman checking a boarding pass on her phone
A departures screen showing one flight as "DELAYED"
A cleaner mopping the floor near a "Wet floor" sign
A man running with a coffee cup in his hand

tasks.label: Task 4: Making Predictions
tasks.prompt: In this picture, what do you think will most probably happen next? Describe what you think will happen to the people and things you see.

tasks.label: Task 5: Comparing and Persuading
tasks.prompt: You and a close friend are planning a weekend away together. Choose the trip you prefer. Then persuade your friend, who prefers the other trip, that your choice is better.

options.title: Lakeside cabin
details: No Wi-Fi; nearest store 20 minutes away

options.title: Downtown hotel in another city
details: Close to museums, restaurants and shopping

tasks.label: Task 6: Dealing with a Difficult Situation
tasks.prompt: Your colleague and friend, Maria, sent an important report to a client with several wrong figures. Your manager has not noticed yet, but the client will review the report on Monday. You have to choose one option. Explain your choice and say what you will tell the person.

options.title: Talk to Maria
details: Tell her about the errors so she can correct them herself
Offer to help her send a corrected version before Monday
Risk: she may feel embarrassed or defensive

options.title: Talk to your manager
details: Make sure the problem is handled properly before the client sees it
Risk: Maria may feel you betrayed her trust

tasks.label: Task 7: Expressing Opinions
tasks.prompt: Some school boards are considering a four-day school week, with longer school days, to save money. Do you think this is a good idea? Explain your reasons.
points: Effects on students' learning and energy
Effects on working parents and childcare
Whether the savings are worth it

tasks.label: Task 8: Describing an Unusual Situation
tasks.prompt: You are in a second-hand furniture store and see an unusual chair. Your sister is looking for furniture for her new apartment. Call her and describe the chair in detail so that she can decide whether she wants it.

scene.caption: An unusual chair in a second-hand furniture store

items.label: A chair shaped like a giant open hand, with the fingers as the backrest
Covered in bright yellow velvet
Four small wheels instead of legs
A hidden drawer under the seat, big enough for books
A tiny reading lamp attached to the thumb
About as wide as a small sofa
A price tag: $95, "slightly worn"
